article.hook: Someone says, "I just need to finish one more thing," but the list never ends. The South Node in Capricorn asks us to notice when commitment becomes a cage, not a cause.
article.lived: For nearly two years, we keep showing up to the same meetings, filing the same reports, and defending the same status markers. Tasks that once felt like achievements start to wear thin, yet the impulse to push harder sticks around. You see it in the way we reset goals without changing direction, like running laps inside a glass box. The routine is familiar and the weight of duty feels like a habit that’s harder to drop than a phone.
article.turn: The hard edge is that chasing control through work often means sidestepping what actually needs attention - rest, connection, or letting go. We tighten our grip on roles and titles until they become armor, not identity. Stop proving your worth through how much you can carry; sometimes the strongest move is putting down the burden and stepping back from the grind.
moves: Cancel one recurring obligation you don’t need to carry anymore.
Leave one meeting early and notice how the day shifts without that extra hour.
Say no to one new request that doesn’t serve your current priorities.

notes: closer is long; end on a shorter line with bite
